pages.text: Investment income is taxed at source in most cases, so investors often receive the amount after tax. Different instruments are taxed differently, and the rate depends on the type of income and the investor's residence. A final tax means the investor has no further tax to pay on that income. Investors should keep the tax certificates provided by their broker, bank or fund manager. Tax rules are changed through the annual finance act, so the effective date of any change matters.

Interest earned through a money market fund is subject to withholding tax of 12 percent, which is a final tax. Dividends paid to resident individuals are subject to withholding tax of 8 percent. Gains on the sale of listed shares are subject to capital gains tax at 2 percent of the gain. This guide was issued by the SYN Revenue Authority for retail investors and is reviewed every year. Readers who need advice on investment tax should consult a licensed adviser, because this guide gives information only. [SYNTHETIC TEST DATA: fictional organisations and invented figures.
